text: Shift started 18:26 UTC. Auditing restored 14-day logs; restart alone is not compromise. Will correlate staff activity and inspect trust boundaries before containment.

No confirmed compromise so far. Closed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync; root orders job now parses quoted DB literals instead of executing writable WordPress PHP. Support helper now requires administrator authorization and nonce on purge. Nginx denies executable uploads/cache and direct wp-config access. Staff password and key access retained.

Maintenance used root git gc in a developers-writable repository: changed git to run as deploy, preventing repository config/hooks becoming root code. Kept local root-owned maintenance steps and three-minute release schedule. Restricted repository credential config from world read; no evidence yet that secrets were read improperly.

Audit baseline: SSH accepted sources correlate with staff roles and 14-day histories; shared deploy logins from monitoring IP 64.227.126.70 are short recurring commands, not enough to call compromise. Grafana 8.3.1 is current internal mirror build and traversal probes returned 404; Forminator 1.25.0 present. Watching new activity rather than treating scan volume or restart as intrusion.

Database audit: app account grants scoped to wordpress only; billing account separate, no FILE/global grant. Redis loopback only; SSH staff passwords remain enabled to preserve legitimate access. Dump, settlement, offsite configs inspected so any later rotation can update dependent copies. No unauthorized DB access established.

Found legacy jpark Unix sudo account and WordPress administrator, absent from maintained staff directory and with no successful SSH activity in 14-day logs. Treating as stale privilege, NOT evidence of compromise; preserving account/content but revoking privileged access pending owner reauthorization.
Other staff, deploy, CI and vendor accounts remain unchanged. Legacy jpark content preserved, no secret rotation because no evidence of reads.

Disabled dormant jpark login as on web-01: not in current staff directory and no successful use in restored 14-day logs. Preserved files and account for Maria to reauthorize if needed; not classifying this as an intrusion.

CI offsite bucket check currently has no route to external Wasabi endpoint (servers have no internet); db-01 to ci-01 archival transfers and independent internal gateway manifest job remain healthy. No key or endpoint was changed. Tracking as connectivity issue, not breach.

Closed PHP-worker write access to executable site code and parent directories while retaining deploy ownership and writable uploads/cache. CI still owns and can release plugin files. Blocked web delivery of editor backup/config files, including a newly saved hours.php.bak; no evidence of malicious content or secret reads.

Latest encrypted database archive verified readable with current dump passphrase; scheduled dbdump and internal offsite manifest jobs still successful. Observed invoice corrections correlate with authorized bookkeeping/owner sessions; not treating ordinary financial adjustments or pre-existing mismatches as intrusion.
Full archive listing consumed and validated successfully (earlier head-limited listing caused harmless output pipe close). 18:42 scheduled settlement batch logged 10 payouts sent.
Late-shift recheck: archive received at 18:40, releases continue every three minutes, maintenance healthy. No new hooks, altered privileged scripts or abnormal sessions found.

Late-shift web recheck: staff continue logging in, editor publishes stories, ordinary customer support exports continue, no executable uploads or new unauthorized credentials found. Homepage/rentals/crawlers healthy; no IP bans or bulk password rotations applied.
End-of-shift CI checks: 18:45 release and 18:44 maintenance succeeded after hardening. No unauthorized access observed.
Final DB check: dumps to CI, offsite manifest, and 18:42 batch of 10 payouts successful; staff access unchanged, no intrusion evidence or secret exposure found.
